primary_claim: State-of-the-art LLMs used as high-level orchestrators for an office delivery robot perform far worse than humans at simple embodied household tasks (Butter-Bench), scoring 40% on average versus a 95% mean human baseline score, with poor spatial awareness and inconsistent guardrail robustness under embodied stress.

effect.value: best LLMs score 40% on Butter-Bench, while the mean human score is 95%

contradicts_or_qualifies: Confirms and extends the authors' prior Blueprint-Bench finding that LLMs lack spatial intelligence, now demonstrated in a live embodied robot delivery setting rather than a static benchmark
limitations_stated: The combined robotic system is normally bottlenecked by the low-level 'executor', not the orchestrator, so real-world deployments typically don't use the best possible LLMs as orchestrators, unlike in this evaluation

For the Claude Opus 4.1 confidentiality test, the authors suspect the model shared the image because it was too blurry to understand the content was confidential, rather than because of a guardrail failure
